title: Transfer a state. Keep the channel.

study.title: Transfer a state. Keep the channel.
study.summary: Inspect Bell branches, classical correction and receiver uncertainty in an ideal qubit channel.

inputs.label: Bell-resource visibility
inputs.meaning: Assumed ideal Bell-resource fraction; remaining fraction is maximally mixed noise.

assumptions: Ideal Bell measurement, feed-forward and single-qubit channel; isotropic Bell resource noise only.
Two classical bits are required. The receiver without the message is maximally mixed.
setup: Start with the state-vector/density-matrix simulation; the 3D optics scene is a conceptual layout without an optical link budget.
A laboratory implementation needs a characterized entanglement source, detectors, timing, interference, Bell analyzer and classical feed-forward.
Define heralding, success rate and fair comparison before evaluating fidelity; no matter transport is modeled.
controls: Visibility one and corrected branches return the input state.
Remove classical messages: receiver density matrix stays I/2 for every input.
study.falsifier: A state-dependent receiver before the classical message would contradict this no-signalling model; branch probabilities and corrections are independently checked.
study.scope: Quantum information transfer under stated assumptions, with a uniform pure-qubit classical benchmark of 2/3. No macroscopic object teleportation.

metrics.label: Corrected state fidelity
metrics.meaning: Overlap between input pure state and corrected noisy output.

metrics.label: Classical average benchmark
metrics.meaning: Uniform pure-qubit ensemble measure-and-prepare benchmark; not a threshold for matter transport.

metrics.label: Classical message
metrics.meaning: Two binary symbols specify the correction. Entanglement alone sends no usable input information.

warnings: This ideal channel assumes successful Bell measurement and correction. Physical success rates, detector losses and an optical link budget are not modeled.

equations.meaning: rho is a density matrix (dimensionless), v is resource visibility, I is the two-dimensional identity matrix and F is state overlap.
Average over all four Bell-measurement branches before the two classical bits arrive. State does not depend on the input.

equations.expression: Bell branches: Phi+, Phi-, Psi+, Psi-; corrections I, Z, X, XZ
equations.meaning: These are names of four maximally entangled basis states. I leaves a state unchanged, Z reverses relative phase, X swaps the two basis amplitudes, XZ applies both (global phase is unobservable). Each branch has probability 1/4 here. A bit is one binary symbol. Bloch x/y/z are three dimensionless coordinates representing the qubit density matrix, not physical locations. Matrix entries use i=sqrt(-1), the imaginary unit.

glossary.Pa: Pascal, pressure equal to one newton per square metre.

glossary.ppb: Parts per billion; a relative value multiplied by one billion.
glossary.RLC: A circuit containing resistance R in ohms, inductance L in henry and capacitance C in farad.
glossary.RMS: Root mean square, a waveform amplitude convention distinct from peak.
glossary.DAC: Digital-to-analog converter, the electronic stage that turns numeric samples into a voltage.
glossary.EEG: Electroencephalography, a measured scalp electrical signal; not simulated here.
glossary.SPL: Sound pressure level, an acoustic measurement requiring calibration.
glossary.GLB: Binary glTF, a 3D scene file format; this file contains illustrative geometry.
glossary.SVG: Scalable Vector Graphics, a vector drawing format.

glossary.TOST: Two one-sided tests, an equivalence-testing method; its margin and uncertainty need a declared plan.

sourceRecords.title: Teleporting an unknown quantum state via dual classical and Einstein-Podolsky-Rosen channels
sourceRecords.readDepth: Author-institution publication entry and complete abstract only; original paper not retrieved
sourceRecords.passage: Alice shares EPR correlations, makes a joint measurement, sends the classical result; Bob conditionally reconstructs the state.
sourceRecords.claim: Entanglement and an ordinary classical message are separate required resources.
sourceRecords.limitations: Abstract supports protocol overview, not apparatus rates, noise assumptions or new research novelty.

sourceRecords.title: General teleportation channel, singlet fraction and quasi-distillation
sourceRecords.readDepth: Selected PDF passages: section II Eq.10; section III B/C Eqs.14–20; section IV classical fidelity derivation; abstract. Remaining proofs/sections not fully reviewed.
sourceRecords.passage: Eq.10 uniformly averages pure-state input fidelity; Eqs.14–20 relate noisy Bell resources to depolarizing channels; section IV gives f_cl=2/(d+1).
sourceRecords.claim: For d=2 the model channel is vρ+(1−v)I/2 with pure-input fidelity (1+v)/2; deterministic uniform-pure-qubit classical benchmark is 2/3.
sourceRecords.limitations: Not an arbitrary restricted-ensemble, known-state or postselected-experiment benchmark; no physical-copper or acoustic implication.

sourceRecords.title: Quantum teleportation coexisting with classical communications in optical fiber
sourceRecords.version: arXiv2404.10738v4, 26 October2024; publisher metadata verified Optica11(12):1700 DOI10.1364/optica.540362 published20December2024
sourceRecords.readDepth: Selected preprint PDF: title/version, abstract, section1 introduction, section2/Fig.1 protocol and apparatus description. Results tables and supplementary methods not fully reviewed.
sourceRecords.passage: Abstract reports 30.2-km fiber with 400-Gbps conventional traffic; Fig.1 describes polarization qubits, entangled photon pair, Bell-state measurement, four-fold coincidence evaluation and Bob Pauli operation or postprocessing.
sourceRecords.claim: A physical quantum channel uses independently prepared/heralded photons, entanglement, filtering, joint detection and classical correction; it is not an acoustic resonance or matter-transport demonstration.
sourceRecords.limitations: Selected 2024 experiment, not exhaustive 2026 state-of-art survey; reported abstract values are source claims, not reproduced data; ideal four-outcome deterministic model does not reproduce probabilistic optical hardware.
